picks.style: late antique latin epithalamium, lyre and reed pipes, low male chorus under a high solo voice, torchlit processional, stately, uncanny
picks.why: The wedding hymn sung by the dead under Pluto's roof — a complete, self-contained marriage blessing in the underworld.

picks.style: latin pastoral hymn, panpipes, harp, kithara, bright female voice with soft choir, unhurried, flowering, building
picks.why: Zephyrus' prayer and the flower-gathering in Henna: pure sensory spring, with Hyacinthus and Narcissus woven in as omens.

picks.style: orphic invocation, solo lyre, sustained drone, warm baritone, slow, spellbound, gathering
picks.why: Orpheus lays down his lyre and nature turns savage again; when he takes it up, wolves lie down with lambs — the poem's own myth of song.

picks.style: greek tragic monody, aulos, frame drum, keening female voice, rubato, funereal, raw
picks.why: Electra's night-lament for her father — repetition, self-wounding, and a direct address to the dead: built to be wailed.

picks.style: ancient tragic chorus, low drums, aulos drone, layered voices, dark, inexorable, slow build
picks.why: The matricide heard from offstage, the chorus turning it into judgment: no house more pitiable than the race of Tantalus.

picks.style: greek victory ode, kithara, lyre, hand drum, layered female chorus, dancing, celebratory with an undertow
picks.why: The garlanding of Orestes — a genuine victory ode with dance, crown, and shout, before the horror lands.

picks.style: georgian satirical ballad, harpsichord, cello, plucked strings, wry baritone, brisk, declamatory
picks.why: The sermon of Prudence — keep up appearances, sin in secret, vice is virtue when well concealed. Perfectly quotable hypocrisy.

picks.style: grim georgian broadside ballad, fiddle, snare drum, stern male voice, marching tempo, bitter
picks.why: Empire indicted in couplets: she explains the worth of freedom while loading their necks with chains.

picks.style: 18th century english declamatory air, chamber organ, viola da gamba, insistent tenor, measured, accusatory
picks.why: The hammering anaphora of 'Think' — a whole argument driven by one repeated imperative.

picks.style: georgian pastoral ballad, baroque strings, harpsichord continuo, clear soprano, lilting, plaintive
picks.why: Colin as breeze, as flower, as stream — a whole ballad of comparisons with its own built-in refrain.

picks.style: english drawing-room song, lute and viol, light tenor, gentle, teasing, chamber
picks.why: A neat, complete conceit: worshipping Chloe's likeness in another woman — idol-worship, have mercy on me.

picks.style: english pastoral hymn, chamber organ, viol consort, warm tenor, unhurried, domestic, contented
picks.why: The country parson's household in Spenserian stanzas — two roses on one stalk, and seasons that change without changing them.

picks.style: scots folk song, fiddle, small pipes, guitar, warm male voice with a lilt, walking pace, open air
picks.why: Now Westlin Winds: the evening walk with Peggy, internal rhyme throughout, already half a song on the page.

picks.style: scots lament ballad, solo fiddle, bodhran, grave male voice, slow, refrain-driven
picks.why: Man was made to mourn — a true recurring refrain, the most singable structure in the whole set.

picks.style: scots tavern ballad, fiddle and cittern, buoyant baritone, brisk, wry, defiant
picks.why: Fate snapping the brittle thread, then the turn: this life is a' enchanted fairy-land, heave care o'er-side.

picks.style: hellenistic elegy, low aulos, kithara, layered female voices, sparse, mournful, slow
picks.why: Byblis weeping more thickly than the nightingales' brood, then the headband on the oak — a compact, devastating arc.

picks.style: greek narrative lament, plain male voice over lyre and hand drum, austere, cold, inevitable
picks.why: The girl who opened her city's gates for Achilles and got a wedding of stones — a whole tragedy in fifteen lines.

picks.style: georgian hymn tune, chamber organ, string quartet, earnest male choir, measured, hopeful, congregational
picks.why: Trade as the golden girdle of the globe — the one passage here that is verse rather than lecture, and it sings like a hymn.

picks.style: solemn enlightenment art song, fortepiano, cello, dark baritone, sparse, unsettled, slow
picks.why: The gods toss all life into confusion and mix everything with its reverse — a single unnerving sentence about worship born of ignorance.
